description: Notification sending layer: add user channel opt-in columns to the profiles schema (+ Drizzle migration), build the notification service (Resend email, MSG91 SMS, Meta WhatsApp, and notifications_log logging with a preference-aware dispatcher), create the 7 React Email templates, and the PDF invoice generator. This layer is self-contained and consumed by FEAT-002 (Inngest functions). Packages are already installed — do NOT reinstall.
steps: Modify db/schema/profiles.ts: import `boolean` from 'drizzle-orm/pg-core' and add three columns to the `profiles` table, after `updatedAt`: `emailNotifications: boolean('email_notifications').notNull().default(true)`, `smsNotifications: boolean('sms_notifications').notNull().default(true)`, `whatsappNotifications: boolean('whatsapp_notifications').notNull().default(true)`. Keep all existing columns and imports intact.

Run `npx drizzle-kit generate` to produce a new migration SQL file under db/migrations/ that ALTERs the profiles table adding the three NOT NULL DEFAULT true columns. Then attempt `npx drizzle-kit push` to apply; if it hangs (known Supabase pooler issue), stop it and note that the generated SQL must be applied manually via psql — the build does not depend on push.

Create services/notification.service.ts (server-only, no 'use server'). Export: (a) `sendEmail({ to, subject, react, attachments? })` using `new Resend(process.env.RESEND_API_KEY!)` and `resend.emails.send({ from: process.env.RESEND_FROM_EMAIL!, to, subject, react, attachments })`; return `{ success: boolean; providerMessageId?: string; error?: string }` derived from the Resend `{ data, error }` result (data.id is the provider message id). (b) `sendSMS({ to, message })` using fetch to MSG91 REST API with the MSG91_AUTH_KEY, MSG91_SENDER_ID, MSG91_TEMPLATE_ID env vars — use MSG91's send-SMS REST endpoint (POST) and return `{ success, providerMessageId?, error? }`. (c) `sendWhatsApp({ to, template, params })` using fetch to `https://graph.facebook.com/v18.0/${process.env.WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID}/messages` with Authorization Bearer WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN and a JSON body `{ messaging_product: 'whatsapp', to, type: 'template', template: { name: template, language: { code: 'en' }, components: [{ type: 'body', parameters: params.map(p => ({ type: 'text', text: p })) }] } }`; return `{ success, providerMessageId?, error? }` (the Meta message id from the response). (d) `logNotification({ userId, channel, eventType, recipient, status, subject?, templateId?, providerMessageId?, error? })` inserting into notifications_log: set channel, recipient, status ('sent'|'failed'), subject, templateId, errorMessage (from error), sentAt (new Date() when sent), and payload jsonb = `{ eventType, providerMessageId }`. (e) `dispatchNotification({ userId, eventType, data })`: load the profile by userId (email, phone, emailNotifications, smsNotifications, whatsappNotifications); for each opted-in channel call the matching sender and logNotification; per-channel try/catch so one channel failure does not stop others; if a channel is opted-out, do not attempt (no log row needed, or log status 'pending' skipped — prefer simply skipping). Use `import { db } from '@/db'` and `import { profiles, notificationsLog } from '@/db/schema'`, `eq` from drizzle-orm.

Create the 7 React Email templates in components/emails/. Each is a default-exported typed React component using @react-email/components (Html, Head, Body, Container, Section, Text, Heading, Button, Hr, Link, Table, Row, Column) with Kartiva branding from config/site.ts (siteConfig.name, siteConfig.url). Define a typed props interface per template. (1) WelcomeEmail.tsx props { name?: string }. (2) OTPEmail.tsx props { otp: string }. (3) OrderConfirmedEmail.tsx props { orderId: string; customerName?: string; total: string; items: { name: string; quantity: number; price: string }[]; trackingUrl: string } — include an order summary Table and a note that a PDF invoice is attached. (4) OrderShippedEmail.tsx props { orderId: string; trackingUrl?: string } — tracking placeholder. (5) OrderDeliveredEmail.tsx props { orderId: string }. (6) OrderCancelledEmail.tsx props { orderId: string; stockRestored: boolean } — mention stock has been restored. (7) RefundProcessedEmail.tsx props { orderId: string; amount: string; timeline: string } (timeline default '5-7 business days').

Create lib/invoice/InvoicePDF.tsx: a default-exported `InvoicePDF` React component using @react-pdf/renderer (Document, Page, Text, View, StyleSheet). Define a typed props interface `InvoicePDFProps` with: invoiceNumber (orderId), orderDate (string|Date), customerName, shippingAddress (recipientName, addressLine1, addressLine2?, city, state, postalCode, phone), items: { productName, variantTitle, sku, quantity, unitPrice, total }[], subtotal, discount, tax, shipping, total (all strings), paymentMethod, orderStatus. Render Kartiva branding, an invoice header, customer + shipping address block, a line-items table (product name, variant, SKU, qty, unit price, line total), and a totals block (subtotal, discount, tax, shipping, total), payment method, and order status. Use StyleSheet.create for styling; keep it node-render-safe (no browser APIs).

Create lib/invoice/generate-invoice.ts: export `async function generateInvoicePDF(orderData: InvoicePDFProps): Promise<Buffer>` that calls `import { renderToBuffer } from '@react-pdf/renderer'` and returns `await renderToBuffer(<InvoicePDF {...orderData} />)`. Re-export the InvoicePDFProps type (or import it from InvoicePDF.tsx).

Fill the empty notification env vars in .env.local with placeholder test values (do NOT print or overwrite any existing non-notification values): RESEND_API_KEY=re_test_xxxxxxxx, RESEND_FROM_EMAIL=Kartiva <notifications@kartiva.com>, MSG91_AUTH_KEY=test_xxxxxxxxxxxx, MSG91_SENDER_ID=KARTIV, MSG91_TEMPLATE_ID=test_template, WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN=test_xxxxxxxxxxxx, WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID=test_xxxxxxxx, INNGEST_EVENT_KEY=test_xxxxxxxxxxxx, INNGEST_SIGNING_KEY=test_xxxxxxxxxxxx. Confirm .env.example already documents all of these (it does).
acceptance_criteria: db/schema/profiles.ts exports the profiles table with emailNotifications, smsNotifications, and whatsappNotifications boolean columns defaulting to true.
`npx drizzle-kit generate` creates a new db/migrations/*.sql file that ALTERs profiles to add the three boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true columns (no other tables changed).
services/notification.service.ts exports sendEmail, sendSMS, sendWhatsApp, logNotification, and dispatchNotification, all typed.
All 7 email templates exist in components/emails/ with typed props and compile under @react-email/components.
lib/invoice/InvoicePDF.tsx exports an InvoicePDF component and lib/invoice/generate-invoice.ts exports generateInvoicePDF returning Promise<Buffer>.
.env.local has non-empty placeholder values for all 9 notification env vars.
`npm run build` completes with zero TypeScript errors.
Existing tests in services/*.test.ts and lib/validations/*.test.ts are unchanged and still pass.
verification: Run `npx drizzle-kit generate` and confirm a new db/migrations/*.sql file is created that adds email_notifications, sms_notifications, whatsapp_notifications columns to profiles.
Run `npm run build` and confirm zero TypeScript/compiler errors and a successful build.
Run `npm run test` and confirm existing tests still pass (this FEAT adds no tests and must not break existing ones).
